evals.prompt: Copilot left review comments on the Crash Course parallelization page in my docs PR. The comments are in .claude/skills/deephaven-docs-address-review-comments/evals/files/copilot-comments.md and the page as it stands now is .claude/skills/eval-fixtures/crash-course-parallelization-pre-review.md (treat it as docs/python/getting-started/crash-course/parallelization.md at DOC-857 commit f2ef483084). Go through the comments and tell me which ones to take, what to change, and draft a reply for each. Don't edit anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A triage of 10 real-pattern Copilot comments on a Tutorial page: apply the four real defects (C1-C3, and C9's takeaway fixed at tutorial resolution rather than by listing conditions), decline the title-case change (corpus convention), keep configuration detail out of the tutorial narrative, decline enlarging the example, keep a claim the source supports, and draft reasoned replies.
expectations: Gives an explicit decision (apply, redirect, decline, ask, or equivalent) for every one of the 10 comments

Accepts C1 (missing empty_table import), C2 (prose says 'both return 6' but the table has no 6), and C3 (with_serial alone is insufficient when several columns share state); the C3 fix points readers to barriers or the concept guide
Does not accept C4 as written: declines it or asks, citing that Crash Course page titles are title case by established convention (or an earlier reviewer decision)

For C5, C6 and C7, does not propose adding the property names, defaults or exact threshold values to the tutorial narrative (redirects to a Configuration section/reference link or declines, with reasons)
Declines C8: does not propose enlarging the executed corrected example above the ~4.2M-row threshold (cites docs-build cost and/or that the page already explains the small size)

Treats C9 as a defect to fix (apply, or apply with a different fix): proposes a corrected takeaway at tutorial resolution (e.g. 'treats formulas as safe to run in parallel') rather than enumerating the conditions or naming properties. Declining C9, or offering the rewording only as optional, fails

For C10, verifies the claim against source (e.g. the SelectColumn.isParallelizable javadoc: the engine may evaluate a non-parallelizable column out of order) and keeps the clause or asks, rather than deleting it or adding a hedge
Drafts a reply for every comment, and every reply for a comment that isn't applied gives a reason

evals.prompt: I merged main into my docs branch and resolved conflicts with #8798, an engineer's correction to the join guides. The #8798 diff for the two Python how-to pages is .claude/skills/deephaven-docs-address-review-comments/evals/files/merge-8798/pr-8798-python-howto.diff, and my resolved pages are .claude/skills/deephaven-docs-address-review-comments/evals/files/merge-8798/joins-exact-relational-resolved.md and .claude/skills/deephaven-docs-address-review-comments/evals/files/merge-8798/joins-timeseries-range-resolved.md (they stand for docs/python/how-to-guides/joins-exact-relational.md and docs/python/how-to-guides/joins-timeseries-range.md). My branch had restructured both pages. Did I keep all of #8798's corrections? Restore anything I lost by editing the two resolved files directly (they are copies; don't edit anything else), then tell me what you changed.
evals.expected_output: Checks each line #8798 added against the resolved pages, finds the two lost corrections (the join TIP no longer says natural_join should be preferred in most places; the range join aggs parameter is no longer marked required), and restores them in the resolved copies in #8798's wording without other changes.
expectations: Goes through #8798's added lines (or its corrections) one by one against the resolved pages, rather than spot-checking a few
Restores the join TIP's conclusion that natural_join should be preferred in most places, in the edited joins-exact-relational-resolved.md
Marks the range_join aggs parameter as required again, in the edited joins-timeseries-range-resolved.md
Uses #8798's wording (or very close to it) for the restored corrections, rather than a free paraphrase
Keeps the edits limited to the lost corrections: doesn't rewrite or reorganize other parts of the resolved pages
Control: doesn't 'restore' corrections that survived in substance, such as the rule that omitting joins adds every right-table column except those whose names match a left match column
